Esta tabela resume cada ponto de gramáti: This table sums up every grammar point from the earlier lessons in one line. Reread one line at a time and say an example of your own out loud. If a line looks strange, go back to the lesson shown or open the topic in the Grammar tab.
Não existe «o/a/um/uma»; o contexto deci: There is no «the / a»; the context decides.
Sem «есть» no presente: «Это дом», «Я вр: No «есть» in the present: «Это дом», «Я врач».
-ы / -и / -а / -я; depois de г к х ж ч ш: -ы / -и / -а / -я; after г к х ж ч ш щ write -и.
Concordam com o gênero e o número do sub: They agree with the gender and number of the noun.
У меня есть + nominativo; У меня нет + g: У меня есть + nominative; У меня нет + genitive.
в = dentro, país, cidade; на = em cima,: в = inside, country, city; на = on top, open space, event; verbs of position.
Parado: preposicional; movimento: acusat: Standing still: prepositional; movement: accusative (в школе → в школу).
Acusativo: -а → -у; masculino e neutro i: Accusative: -а → -у; inanimate masculine and neuter do not change.
Nunca mudam; vêm do adjetivo trocando o: They never change; they come from the adjective by changing the ending to -о.
Sim/não pela entonação; palavra interrog: Yes/no by intonation; the question word goes first.
Seis casos; cada terminação mostra a fun: Six cases; each ending shows the function of the word.
в + dia (в пятницу); в + hora (в пять ча: в + day (в пятницу); в + hour (в пять часов).
Depois de vogal -сь, depois de consoante: After a vowel -сь, after a consonant -ся.

Знакомство / Conhecendo-se: Знакомство / Getting to know each other
Two adults meet at an event.
— Olá! Eu me chamo Paolo. E a senhora?: — Hello! My name is Paolo. And you?
— Eu me chamo Anna. De onde o senhor é?: — My name is Anna. Where are you from?
— Sou da Itália. Moro em Moscou. E a sen: — I am from Italy. I live in Moscow. And you?
— Sou russa. Moro em Moscou. O senhor tr: — I am Russian. I live in Moscow. Do you work?
— Sim, trabalho num escritório. Sou enge: — Yes, I work in an office. I am an engineer.
— Yes, very much! I like this city.

Os 10 erros mais comuns de quem fala por: The 10 most common mistakes of English speakers
Estes dez erros aparecem com mais frequê: These ten mistakes appear most often among English speakers. Fixing only these already makes your speech much more natural. Read each pair out loud: first the wrong one (to recognise the odd sound), then the right one (to fix it in memory).
No «есть» in the present to say "is". (English forces you to say "it is"; Russian does not.)
The possessive agrees with the gender. (English "my" never changes.)
The direct object takes the accusative.
The double negative is compulsory in Russian.
The person who needs goes into the dative.
A question is made by intonation, with no «есть».
